lina (infra): Heads up — after the firewall rewrite at 03:20 UTC we started seeing mass node warmup failures in EU-edge GPU pools. KMS decrypts failing intermittently, nodes repeatedly reprovisioning.

lina (infra): sample kubelet log: `2026-03-20T03:21:05Z error: failed to unwrap keystore: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc=transport is closing`

lina (infra): proto-level errors on keystore path + lots of TCP retransmits in the flow logs. I suspect MTU/fragmentation or conntrack state limits introduced by the new rules.

tia (oncall): dipping in — nice catch. Which fw change exactly? rule-id or commit? :thinking_face:

lina (infra): commit 9d2f4b0 — tightened ESTABLISHED tracking and enabled `drop-invalid` along with a NAT rewrite. Changed MSS clamping policy on the edge NAT.

omar: that fits. KMS traffic can be large TLS handshakes + fragmented packets. If MSS clamp dropped it, we see TLS failures. Also conntrack can evict short-lived entries causing resets.

ben (platform): impact: autoscaler sees pod init failures, scales up new nodes (retry storm), then they hit same error => cost spike. Cloud billing shows a 45% GPU-hour increase in EU edge since 03:22. We should throttle scale or pause autoscaling until fixed.

lina (infra): mitigation plan I propose: 1) revert fw commit (safe) 2) add bypass rule for keystore/KMS on edge to avoid NAT rewrite 3) tune conntrack (`nf_conntrack_max`) and add `MSS clamp` to 1400 for edge-MTU path. Which should we do first?

tia (oncall): revert first, then apply conntrack/MSS as mitigations before re-running the rewrite. Revert looks low-risk.

omar: agree. Also add iptables rule like: ```iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu``` That should fix fragmentation without full rollback. But bypass/KMS whitelist is quickest.

lina (infra): starting rollback now. @deploy-bot can you run rollback-job `fw/rewrite-rollout/9d2f4b0` to canary-edge and then to EU-edge?

deploy-bot: rollback-job queued: fw/rewrite-rollout/9d2f4b0 -> canary-edge. ETA ~3m. Logs will stream to #eng-releases. :gear:
